newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-CRENSHAW AND ZOELLER OUT OF BRITISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CRENSHAW AND ZOELLER OUT OF BRITISH OPEN.

text.p: Ben Crenshaw and Fuzzy Zoeller, two veteran Americans with four major titles between them, have withdrawn from this month's British Open at Royal Troon, it was announced on Friday.

Crenshaw, who won the Masters title in 1984 and 1995, was exempt from final qualifying but has pulled out because of a foot injury and because his father is seriously ill, a spokesman for the organisers said.

Zoeller, the 1979 Masters and 1984 U.S. Open winner, was not exempt and would have had to survive final qualifying to get a place in the Open, which runs from July 17 to 20. He gave no reason for pulling out.
Zoeller made headlines this year with controversial remarks about Tiger Woods after Woods won the Masters in April.
Another American with direct entry into the Open, Fred Funk, has withdrawn with a neck injury.
Others who have pulled out of final qualifying include Americans Duffy Waldorf and Robert Gamez, Australia's Peter Fowler and Germany's Heinz-Peter Thuel.
